mainTopic: Blemishes (מומין) of a בכור: jaw, ears, tails, warts in the eye, and uneven body parts
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story: the חכמים ruled that a בכור whose lower jaw sticks out has a מום. רב פפא explains this is because the jawbone itself sticks out, unlike a person's protruding lip, which is only a מום for a כהן. A new משנה follows. A doubled ear is a מום only if its two parts share one bone (cartilage), and a goat's tail that is pig-like, or a tail with fewer than three joints, is a מום. The גמרא explains that a pig-like tail means a curled one. It also shows that רב הונא misread the three-joint rule: that rule is about a lamb, so a goat needs only two joints. Another משנה lists more blemishes, including a wart in the eye and visibly uneven eyes or ears. After several attempts, the גמרא settles a contradiction about warts. A wart in the black of the eye is a full מום. In the white, a wart with a hair disqualifies the animal from the מזבח and one without a hair does not. The amud ends with a new משנה about a calf's short tail and which leg joint it is measured against.

steps.title: The story of the protruding lower jaw
steps.stepSummary: A בכור animal's lower jaw stuck out past the upper jaw. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asked the חכמים, and they ruled it is a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was also a case where the lower jaw stuck out past the upper jaw. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asked the חכמים, and they said: that is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a story about a בכור animal whose lower jaw stuck out farther than its upper jaw. The חכמים ruled that this counts as a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may not be slaughtered and eaten unless it has a מום. So this ruling has a practical result: an animal with this jaw shape now counts as blemished. The next step will question this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish or physical defect. It lets a בכור be slaughtered outside the Temple.
A story, an actual case that happened

phrases.english: And there was also an incident
where the lower jaw stuck out beyond the upper one,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel asked the Sages
and they said: That is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a version of the משנה from earlier on the daf by adding one more case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור whose lower jaw sticks out past the upper jaw has a מום.

steps.title: But a protruding lip is a blemish only for a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling. A protruding lip is listed as a מום only for a כהן, because the פסוק requires a כהן to look like other כהנים. That requirement does not apply to animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned this about a person: if his upper lip sticks out past the lower, or the lower past the upper, that is a blemish. That rule is for a person, because it is written 'Any man of the seed of Aaron,' meaning a man who looks like the rest of Aaron's descendants. But for an animal it should not be a blemish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling from step 1. It quotes a משנה that lists protruding lips as a מום for a person, and argues that this kind of מום applies only to people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a כהן, the פסוק "איש איש מזרע אהרן" teaches that he must look like other כהנים. So even an odd-looking feature that is not a real defect can disqualify him. Animals have no such rule, so an odd-looking mouth should not be a מום for a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Looks like the rest of Aaron's descendants

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a protruding mouth is never a מום. It is saying that for a person, "looking different" alone counts as a מום, and that idea does not carry over to animals.

phrases.english: But it is regarding a person that we learned:
If his upper lip sticks out beyond the lower one,
or the lower one sticks out beyond the upper one,
that is a blemish.
It is regarding a person that it is written:
"Any man of the seed of Aaron,"
a man who is equal to the seed of Aaron,
phrases.notes: He means a כהן must look like other כהנים, with nothing odd about his appearance.

phrases.english: but with an animal, not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a protruding lower jaw is a מום in a בכור animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Protruding lips are a מום only because of the rule that a כהן must look like other כהנים. That rule applies only to people, so it should not make an animal blemished.

steps.title: רב פפא: bone versus no bone
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the animal case is a jaw where the bone itself sticks out, which is a real מום. The human case is lips with no bone, which is a מום only for a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: There is no difficulty. This case is where there is a bone; that case is where there is no bone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בכור story, the jawbone itself sticks out, which is a real physical defect even in an animal. In the משנה about a person, only the soft lip sticks out with no bone. That is a מום only because a כהן must look like other כהנים. So both rulings stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: A protruding jaw is a מום in an animal only when the bone sticks out. If only the soft lip sticks out with no bone, it is a מום only for a כהן.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is not difficult;
this is where it has a bone,
phrases.notes: "This" is the בכור story, where the jawbone itself sticks out.

phrases.english: that is where it has no bone.
phrases.notes: "That" is the משנה about a person's lips.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different physical situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal's protruding jaw seemed to be the same case as a person's protruding lip, which is a מום only for people.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal case has a bone sticking out, which is a real defect. The human case has no bone and counts as a מום only because of how a כהן looks.

steps.title: New משנה: the goat's doubled ear
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה starts. A young goat whose ear is doubled has a מום only if both parts share one bone (one cartilage).
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a kid's ear was doubled, the חכמים said: when it is one bone, it is a blemish; when it has no bone, it is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a young goat whose ear looks doubled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is again bone. If the doubled ear is joined to the ear by bone, one shared cartilage as the ברייתא in step 6 puts it, it counts as a real growth and a מום. If each part has its own separate cartilage, as רש״י explains, it is not a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: a new section of the משנה begins
Doubled, folded so it looks like two

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If the ear of the kid was doubled,
the Sages said:
When it is one bone, it is a blemish;
phrases.notes: He means the doubled ear is joined to the ear by one shared cartilage. The ברייתא in step 6 says the same: one cartilage is a blemish, two separate ones are not.

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ עֶצֶם — אֵינוֹ מוּם.
phrases.english: when it has no bone, it is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It uses the same idea as רב פפא: bone makes the difference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubled ear whose two parts share one bone (cartilage) is a מום. If they are not one bone, it is not a מום.

steps.title: A pig-like or too-short tail
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן גמליאל rules that a young goat's tail that looks like a pig's tail is a מום, and so is a tail with fewer than three joints. Step 11 shows that this second case is about a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא בן גמליאל says: The tail of a kid that looks like a pig's tail, or that does not have three joints, is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds the opinion of רבי חנניא בן גמליאל about blemishes in a goat's tail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives two separate cases. One is a tail shaped like a pig's tail, which is different from a normal goat's tail. The other is a tail so short that it has fewer than three joints. Either one counts as a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Joints or vertebrae of the tail

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: זְנַב הַגְּדִי שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֶה לְשֶׁל חֲזִיר,
phrases.english: The tail of a kid that looks like that of a pig,
or that does not have three joints,
that is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another blemish case in the same משנה, from a named תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat's tail that looks like a pig's tail is a מום, and so is a tail with fewer than three joints (step 11: this case is about a lamb).

steps.title: A ברייתא on swelling and doubled ears
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a swollen mouth or legs is a מום only if bone causes the swelling. It also rules that doubled ears are a מום with one cartilage, but not with two.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: if the animal's mouth or legs are swollen, and it is just puffed up, that is not a מום. If a bone causes it, that is a מום. If its ears are doubled on one cartilage, that is a מום. If they sit on two cartilages, that is not a מום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section begins by bringing a ברייתא that adds more detail to the kinds of blemishes the משנה discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swelling is judged by its cause. Puffiness from air is temporary and does not count, but extra bone is a permanent change and does count. For doubled ears, the deciding factor is whether there is one cartilage or two.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of wind, meaning simply puffed up

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
If its mouth is swollen and its legs are swollen,
if it is because of wind, it is not a blemish;
phrases.notes: "Wind" here means the swelling is just puffiness, with nothing solid underneath.

phrases.english: if it is because of the bone, this is a blemish.
If its ears are doubled,
with one cartilage, this is a blemish;
with two cartilages, it is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה, adding ברייתא detail on swelling and doubled ears.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swelling counts as a מום only if bone causes it. Doubled ears count as a מום with one cartilage, but not with two.

steps.title: What a pig-like tail means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן גמליאל's rule about a goat's pig-like tail. רב פפא explains that 'pig-like' means curled, even if the tail is thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: a young goat's tail that looks like a pig's tail is a מום. רב פפא said: do not think this means a thin tail. It means a curled tail, even if it is thick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה, and רב פפא explains exactly which feature makes a tail 'like a pig's.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the resemblance to a pig is about thinness. רב פפא says the key feature is the curl. A curled tail is a מום even when it is thick, like a normal goat's tail.

keyTerms.meaning: The tail of a young goat

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא quoting the משנה from step 5, where this view was given in the name of רבי חנניא בן גמליאל.

phrases.aramaic: זְנַב הַגְּדִי שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֶה לְשֶׁל חֲזִיר.
phrases.english: The tail of a young goat that looks like that of a pig.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא תֵּימָא דְּקַטִּינָא,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Do not say it means one that is thin,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דִּכְרִיכָא, אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲלִימָא.
phrases.english: rather one that is curled, even though it is thick.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא תֵּימָא דְּקַטִּינָא, אֶלָּא דִּכְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה (the tail) and defines its terms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pig-like tail means a curled tail, and it is a מום even when thick.

steps.title: רב הונא counts tail joints
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's three-joint rule, רב הונא says a goat's tail with two joints is a מום and with three it is not. A lamb's tail with three joints is a מום and with four it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'or if it does not have three joints.' רב הונא said: for a goat, two joints is a מום and three is not. For a lamb, three is a מום and four is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, and רב הונא gives the joint counts that make a tail too short.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reads the משנה's 'three joints' as the minimum for a goat. For a lamb he sets the minimum one joint higher, at four.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שָׁלֹשׁ חוּלְיוֹת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Or if it does not have three joints, etc.
Rav Huna said: With a young goat,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתַּיִם הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, שָׁלֹשׁ אֵינוֹ מוּם.
phrases.english: two is a blemish, three is not a blemish.
With a lamb, three is a blemish,
four is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the משנה's second tail rule, the number of joints.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat needs three joints and a lamb needs four. Fewer than that is a מום.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives lower joint counts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a goat's tail with one joint is a מום and with two it is not. A lamb's tail with two joints is a מום and with three it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: for a goat, one joint is a מום and two is not. For a lamb, two is a מום and three is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with a ברייתא whose numbers are one lower than his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the ברייתא's count, a goat with two joints is fine and a lamb with three is fine. רב הונא called both of these a מום, so the ברייתא directly contradicts him.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: With a young goat,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, שְׁתַּיִם אֵינוֹ מוּם.
phrases.english: one is a blemish, two is not a blemish.
With a lamb, two is a blemish,
three is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's numbers.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's joint counts for a goat and a lamb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא sets each minimum one joint lower, so cases רב הונא calls a מום are not a מום.

steps.title: רב הונא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב הונא's view is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the ברייתא defeats רב הונא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered for רב הונא, so his numbers are rejected. The ברייתא's counts stand: two joints for a goat and three for a lamb.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rav Huna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge as decisive.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A goat's tail needs two joints and a lamb's tail needs three. רב הונא's higher numbers are rejected.

steps.title: How the משנה misled רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב הונא's mistake. He assumed the משנה's second clause, like its first, was about a goat, but it is really about a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה misled רב הונא. He thought that since the first part is about a goat, the second part is also about a goat. But that is not so: the first part is about a goat, and the second part is about a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא made his error and gives the correct reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's 'three joints' is really the minimum for a lamb, which fits the ברייתא. רב הונא treated it as the goat's number and then added one for the lamb. That is why both of his numbers came out too high.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's pig-like tail rule is about a goat, but its 'three joints' rule is about a lamb. So a goat needs two joints and a lamb needs three.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume both halves of the משנה's tail rule talk about the same animal. That is exactly the trap רב הונא fell into.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna, the mishna misled him;
he thought: since the first clause is about a young goat,
the latter clause is also about a young goat.
But it is not so.
The first clause is about a young goat, and the latter clause is about a lamb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the refutation, explains the source of רב הונא's error and fixes the reading of the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's first clause (pig-like tail) is about a goat, and its second clause (three joints) is about a lamb.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס lists more blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more blemishes: a wart in the eye, damaged leg bones, a dislocated jaw, and uneven eyes or ears that can be seen by looking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says these are blemishes: a wart in the eye, a damaged bone in a front or back leg, a dislocated jawbone, and one eye or one ear bigger than the other. The difference must be visible by looking, not only by measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It adds a list of blemishes in the name of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item makes the animal a בעל מום. For uneven eyes or ears there is a limit: the difference must be obvious to the eye. If you can only find it with a measuring tool, it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: By sight, noticeable just by looking
By measurement, found only by measuring

phrases.english: MISHNA
Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
one that has a wart in its eyes,
and one whose foreleg or hind leg bone was damaged,
and one whose mouth bone was dislocated,
one of its eyes large and one small,
one of its ears large and one small,
when seen by sight, but not when found only by measurement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the discussion of tail joints ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wart in the eye, damaged leg bones, a dislocated jaw, and visibly uneven eyes or ears are all blemishes.

steps.title: רבי יהודה adds uneven testicles, but the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says it is a blemish if one testicle is twice the size of the other. The חכמים do not agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if one of the animal's two testicles is as big as two of the other, it is a blemish. The חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with one more suggested blemish from רבי יהודה, and the חכמים reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats a big size difference between the testicles like the uneven eyes and ears just listed. The חכמים do not count it as a מום, so the animal stays unblemished according to them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages did not agree with him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
its two testicles,
if one is as large as two of the other,
but the Sages did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a disputed item to the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה counts very uneven testicles as a blemish. The חכמים do not.

steps.title: Is a wart really a blemish? Another משנה says otherwise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a wart can be a מום when another משנה lists a wart among the things that do not allow slaughtering a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean a wart is a blemish? But another משנה contradicts it: these are blemishes for which we do not slaughter, not in the מקדש and not anywhere else: an animal with boils and an animal with a wart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's first item, the wart, by quoting another משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה treats a wart as a real מום. The other משנה lists a wart as something that is not a full blemish, so a בכור with only a wart may not be slaughtered for it. Both cannot be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: here is a source that seems to say the opposite
The rest of the country, outside the מקדש
An animal with boils or a skin disease

phrases.english: GEMARA
Is this to say that a wart is a blemish?
But raise a contradiction:
and these are the ones for which we do not slaughter
not in the Temple and not in the country:
one with boils and one with a wart!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first item of the משנה from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that a wart in the eye is a blemish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה says a wart is not a full blemish for slaughtering a בכור, which contradicts our משנה.

steps.title: The Torah itself calls a wart a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: how can a wart not be a blemish when the תורה lists it as one?
steps.simpleTranslation: And how can you think a wart is not a blemish? A wart is written in the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the idea that a wart is never a blemish, because the תורה names a wart in its list of blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other משנה cannot mean that every wart is not a blemish, because the פסוק lists a wart as a מום. So the question is not which משנה is right. Both kinds of wart must exist, and we need to find the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? It pushes back on an assumption

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not attacking our משנה. It shows that the other משנה cannot mean every wart, because the תורה itself calls a wart a blemish.

phrases.english: And how can you think so?
A wart is written in the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea in step 14 that a wart is simply not a blemish.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the other משנה means a wart is never a blemish.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תורה explicitly lists a wart as a blemish, so some warts must be blemishes.

steps.title: First answer: a wart on the body versus a wart in the eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the other משנה means a wart on the body, while our משנה and the תורה mean a wart in the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no contradiction. That משנה is about a wart on the body, and this one is about a wart in the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle the contradiction by saying each source is about a wart in a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wart in the eye is a real מום, which fits our משנה's words "in its eyes." A wart on the body is not a full blemish, which explains the other משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one... that one; each source is about a different case

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
that one is on its body,
this one is in its eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּגוּפוֹ, הָא בְּעֵינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 14 in light of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by where the wart is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seemed to disagree about every wart.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wart in the eye is a blemish, and a wart on the body is not.

steps.title: The פסוק does not split body from eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the פסוק just says "wart" with no details, so there is no reason to treat the body differently from the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look, the פסוק is written without details. What difference does it make to me if it is on the body or in the eye?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first answer because the תורה gives no basis for splitting warts by location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says "wart" in general. If a wart is a blemish, it should be a blemish wherever it is, so the body-versus-eye split has no source.

keyTerms.meaning: Look now; since it is so
What difference does it make whether... or...

phrases.english: Now, the verse is unspecified,
what difference is it to me if on its body
and what difference is it to me if in its eye?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי קְרָא סְתָמָא, מָה לִי בְּגוּפוֹ וּמָה לִי בְּעֵינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that splits warts into body and eye.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names a wart without saying where it is, so location cannot decide whether it is a blemish.

steps.title: Second answer: a wart with a bone versus one without
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: the difference depends on whether the wart has a bone in it, not where it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no contradiction. This one is a wart that has a bone, and that one is a wart that has no bone.
steps.whatsHappening: After the body-versus-eye answer fails, the גמרא gives a new way to resolve the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new split depends on what the wart is like, so the plain פסוק can still apply anywhere on the animal. A wart with a bone is the real blemish the תורה means. A wart without a bone is the kind the other משנה says does not allow slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: That does not have in it

steps.whatToRemember: This answer splits warts by bone, not by location. Step 19 spells out how it works, and step 20 challenges it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this one is where it has a bone,
phrases.notes: This is the wart the תורה calls a blemish.

phrases.english: that one is where it has no bone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאִית בַּהּ עֶצֶם, הָא דְּלֵית בַּהּ עֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 16 after the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by what the wart is like (bone or no bone)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the difference was where the wart is, body or eye.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wart with a bone is a blemish. A wart without a bone is not always a full blemish (step 19 spells this out).

steps.title: Spelling out the bone distinction
steps.stepSummary: The wart in the פסוק has a bone, and the wart in the other משנה has no bone. A boneless wart in the eye is a מום, but on the body it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wart in the פסוק is one with a bone. The wart in the other משנה is one without a bone. A boneless wart in the eye is a blemish. On the body it is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the answer from step 18 and spelling out exactly how the bone rule works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wart with a bone is a full מום, which is what the פסוק means. A wart without a bone is a full מום only in the eye. On the body it is not a full מום, though it still keeps the animal off the מזבח, which is what the other משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: That of the פסוק (the one the verse speaks about)

phrases.english: The one in the verse — it has a bone in it;
the one in the משנה — it has no bone in it;
phrases.notes: This is the other משנה from step 14, the one that lists a wart as something that does not allow slaughtering a בכור.

phrases.english: in its eye — it is a blemish;
on the body — it is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 18 by spelling out how it works.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case by physical feature (bone or no bone)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between the sources was only about location (eye or body).
steps.terutzMaskana: A wart with a bone is always a מום. A boneless wart is a מום in the eye but not on the body.

steps.title: A boneless wart on the body is just hanging flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a boneless wart on the body should disqualify the animal at all, since רבי אליעזר says hanging flesh does not disqualify an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a boneless wart on the body really disqualified? It is just hanging flesh. We learned that רבי אליעזר says people with hanging flesh are disqualified, but animals with it are fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 19. It quotes a משנה showing that a boneless wart on the body should not disqualify an animal at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said a boneless wart on the body is not a full מום but still keeps the animal off the מזבח. A boneless wart is just a hanging piece of flesh, and רבי אליעזר rules that hanging flesh leaves an animal fit. So that kind of wart should not disqualify the animal at all.

phrases.english: And one with no bone, on the body, is disqualified?
It is merely hanging flesh,
as we learned in a משנה:
רבי אליעזר says:
Those with hanging flesh are disqualified in a person
and are fit in an animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the bone answer from steps 18 and 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a boneless wart on the body disqualifies the animal from the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A boneless wart is just hanging flesh, and רבי אליעזר rules that hanging flesh leaves an animal fit.

steps.title: Both are in the eye: black versus white
steps.stepSummary: New answer: both sources are about a wart in the eye. Our משנה means the black of the eye, and the other משנה means the white.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both are talking about a wart in the eye, and there is no difficulty. This one is in the black part, and that one is in the white part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the bone answer and offers a fresh one. Both sources are about the eye, but different parts of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wart in the black (the pupil) is a full מום, as in our משנה. A wart in the white only disqualifies the animal from the מזבח, as in the other משנה. Now the difference depends on which part of the eye the wart is on.

keyTerms.meaning: The black part of the eye
The white part of the eye

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are in its eye,
and it is not difficult:
this one is in the black,
phrases.notes: This one is our משנה, where the wart is a full מום.

phrases.english: that one is in the white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the bone answer that step 20 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case by location within the eye
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference depended on bone or no bone.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wart in the black of the eye is a full מום. A wart in the white only disqualifies the animal from the מזבח.

steps.title: There are no blemishes in the white
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that there is an established rule that nothing in the white of the eye counts as a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are no blemishes in the white of the eye!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the black/white answer with a known rule about the white of the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing in the white is a blemish, then a wart in the white should not disqualify the animal at all. So the other משנה cannot be talking about the white.

keyTerms.meaning: There are no blemishes in the white of the eye

phrases.english: But there are no blemishes in the white!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the black/white answer from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a wart in the white disqualifies the animal from the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known rule says nothing in the white of the eye is a blemish at all.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a hair makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: Both the rule about the white and the other משנה are about the white of the eye. ריש לקיש explains that a wart with a hair disqualifies, and one without a hair does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both are talking about the white of the eye. ריש לקיש said: there is no difficulty. This one has a hair in it, and that one has no hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the black/white idea but resolves the clash inside the white using ריש לקיש's distinction about a hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other משנה, which says the animal is disqualified from the מזבח, is about a wart in the white that has a hair. The rule 'no blemishes in the white' is about a wart there with no hair. Our משנה, where the wart is a full מום, is still about the black of the eye.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the two sources fit together)

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: a wart in the black of the eye is a full מום. A wart in the white with a hair keeps the animal off the מזבח. A wart in the white without a hair does not matter at all.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'both' here is not our משנה and the other משנה. It is the other משנה and the rule 'no blemishes in the white.' Our משנה stays in the black of the eye.

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are in the white,
and ריש לקיש said: it is not difficult:
this one has a hair in it,
phrases.notes: This is the case where the animal is disqualified from the מזבח.

phrases.english: that one has no hair in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בַּלָּבָן, וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by splitting the white-of-the-eye cases by whether there is a hair.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case by physical feature (hair or no hair)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any wart in the white would contradict 'no blemishes in the white.'
steps.terutzMaskana: In the white, a wart with a hair disqualifies the animal from the מזבח, and one without a hair does not.

steps.title: How big is 'large' and how small is 'small'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of one eye large and one small. A ברייתא says large means like a calf's eye and small means like a goose's eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One of its eyes is large,' etc. It was taught: large means like a calf's eye, and small means like a goose's eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה and brings a ברייתא that defines its words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists unequal eyes as a מום but does not say how unequal. The ברייתא gives a measure: one eye as big as a calf's, or as small as a goose's.

phrases.english: 'One of its eyes is large,' etc.
It was taught:
'Large' means like that of a calf,
'small' means like that of a goose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Large' means an eye as big as a calf's, and 'small' means an eye as small as a goose's.

steps.title: How big a difference do the רבנן allow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about uneven ears and testicles, and asks how big a difference the רבנן allow without calling it a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One of its ears is large, etc.' According to the רבנן, up to how much of a difference between the two testicles is allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line in the משנה and asks a question to clarify it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה said that if one testicle is twice the size of the other, it is a מום, and the רבנן disagreed. So the גמרא wants to know: if double is not enough for the רבנן, how big a difference do they still allow?

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the ones who disagree with רבי יהודה
Up to how much? (asking for a limit)
Etc. (the rest of the quoted line)

phrases.english: One of its ears is large, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of that משנה line, including רבי יהודה's view about testicles. That is what the question is about.

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis, up to how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the eye-size line of the משנה to the next line, about ears and testicles.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How big a size difference between the two testicles the רבנן allow before it counts as a מום.

steps.title: Even a bean-sized second testicle is fine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אחרים: even if the smaller testicle is only the size of a bean, the animal is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: אחרים say that even if the second testicle is no bigger than a bean, the animal is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. According to the רבנן, even a very large difference is not a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said a difference of double is already a מום. This ברייתא shows how far the other side goes: even when one testicle is tiny, as small as a bean, the animal stays כשר. So for the רבנן the difference can be very large: even a bean-sized second testicle does not make the animal blemished.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name used for a particular תנא

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, uneven testicles are not a מום, even if one is as small as a bean.

phrases.english: It is taught: Others say:
Even if the second one is not
more than a bean — the animal is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even if the smaller testicle is only bean-sized, the animal is still fit.

steps.title: A calf's tail that does not reach the leg joint
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a calf whose tail does not reach the leg joint has a מום. The חכמים explain that every calf's tail reaches that joint, and it only grows longer as the calf grows.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A calf's tail that does not reach the ערקוב (leg joint). The חכמים said: it is a blemish, because all calves grow this way, with the tail reaching that joint, and as they keep growing, their tails stretch even longer.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a calf whose tail is too short to reach the leg joint. The חכמים rule that this is a מום, because a normal calf's tail reaches that joint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רש״י explains the reason the חכמים give: a normal calf's tail already reaches the ערקוב, and as the calf grows it stretches even further down. So a tail that falls short of that joint is a defect, a מום. This brings up the next question: which joint is the ערקוב?

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The tail of a calf that does not reach the leg joint,
the Sages said:
all growth of calves is like this;

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיְּהוּ מְגַדְּלִין — הֵן נִמְתָּחוֹת.
phrases.english: as long as they grow, they stretch out.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the tails. They keep getting longer as the calf grows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of uneven body parts ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A calf's tail that does not reach the ערקוב is a מום, because a normal calf's tail reaches it and only stretches further as the calf grows.

steps.title: Which leg joint is meant
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks which ערקוב it means. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says it is the joint in the middle of the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which ערקוב did they mean? רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: the joint that is in the middle of the thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines the word ערקוב that it just used. It names the exact joint the tail is measured against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's leg has more than one joint, so 'the leg joint' is not clear by itself. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס pins it down as the joint in the middle of the thigh. This tells us the exact point the tail is measured against.
steps.whatToRemember: The ערקוב in this משנה is the joint in the middle of the thigh. That is the point the calf's tail is measured against.

phrases.english: Which is the leg joint that they spoke of?
Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
The leg joint that is in the middle of the thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the word ערקוב used in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערקוב is the joint in the middle of the thigh.
